skeptic.objection: The owner is not a 27-year holder. It is one of five new KKR affiliate LLCs that took over a Fairburn industrial portfolio in September 2025: the Development Authority of Fulton County minutes approve assigning the 7250 Graham Road bond project to an LLC with this parcel's owner name, to affiliates of KKR, from an industrial trust that Clarion Partners appeared for. The county parcel layer puts that built 254,000 sq ft warehouse right beside this parcel, and the same owner also holds a 4.3 ac vacant lot at 0 Oakley Rd next to it. So the parcel looks like excess or expansion land that an institutional investor bought about 14 months ago with the neighbouring building. The screener also found no fit for the smallest building envelope here, so its likely use is yard, trailer parking or expansion for that same owner. The 'same owner for 27 years' and long-hold seller signals in the brief rest on a stale 1999 deed. Nothing shows the land is unavailable, but a person should expect a recent buyer who may not sell, and confirm it first.

claims.text: In September 2025 the Development Authority of Fulton County approved assigning the 2003 bond projects, among them 7250 Graham Road, from LIT/Hodges Industrial Trust to five LLCs. One of them has the same name as this parcel's owner in the county record. (This is read from the authority's minutes. The authority was not searched by owner name: the page came from a search on the street address 7250 Graham Road.)

claims.text: The same minutes say the portfolio (about $70 million invested and a million square feet developed) was being assigned to affiliates of KKR. So this parcel's owner looks like a recent institutional buyer, about 14 months ago, not a 1999 holder.

open_items: plans-1 is disputed only in part. Its claim text says M-2 is among the Industrial category's appropriate zoning districts, but the quote lists only development types. The page text after the quote reads 'o&i, c-2, m-1,' and is cut off there, so M-2 is not shown in what was checked. Read the full line on plan page 144.

Pull the current deed and the DAFC fact sheet for the September 2025 assignment. Confirm that this 9.55 ac parcel (0 Graham Rd) went to the KKR affiliate in that 2025 portfolio purchase, and whether it is tied to the 7250 Graham Road bond project (expansion land, parking or stormwater for that building) or is free-standing excess land.

The brief's 'same owner for 27 years' (1999 deed) and 'owner mails from out of state' signals should not be read as long-hold seller motivation. The county yearly-sales layers for 2018 to 2022 returned no sale in a box around this parcel; the 2025 transfer may not be in those layers yet, or was not a qualified sale.

The brief's building-fit check found no placement for the smallest 400 x 445 ft envelope. Together with the same owner's warehouse next door, the parcel's realistic use may be yard, trailer parking or expansion for that building, and its most likely buyer may be the owner itself. A person should ask whether the owner would sell it on its own.
Check for Southpark private covenants or an owners' association (recorded declaration) that limit use, access or outdoor storage on this parcel.
Seen, not verifiable: one web search (on the street address) returned a LoopNet property record for this parcel id among its results. It was not opened or used, and LoopNet is off limits.
